summary: Both operator keystrokes landed between the test phase and this consult, and the slice is now provable end to end rather than owed: IaC/Charts #1 is SUCCESS with registry:5000/charts-home carrying tags `1` and `latest`, HelmCharts was pushed by the operator as 3770fdf (rebased onto e87150d, clearing the non-fast-forward card) and deployed by IaC/HelmCharts #5773 SUCCESS, and charts-prd runs deployment.apps/charts 1/1. I re-verified the three criteria the test phase left owed by execution: `curl https://charts.home/index.yaml` without `-k` returns 200 behind a leaf issued by `O=homelab-ca` with SANs `DNS:charts, DNS:charts.home` (V12/V13), and `helm repo add https://charts.home` + `helm search repo -l` resolves homelab-shared 0.1.0 whose served tarball is sha256-identical to the committed dist/ tarball and to the index's digest field (V14) — verification.json now records all 19 items verified. R1-R5 and every ruling are delivered by P1-P4 with implementing work I can point at, no done-record admits a leftover, and nothing depends on something no phase produced, so there is no work that clears the blocking bar. Mechanical residue fixed and committed in this session: the P4 done-record bullet the r3 reviewer flagged as falsified by its own fix commit (it attributed check 1's completeness to an *empty* scratch store rather than to git not carrying the path, contradicting the same record's :470-472 and tests/publish.sh:92-93).
cards: HelmCharts: `resolve-helm-args prd/charts .` is no longer runnable from this pod now that charts-prd exists — the namespace-exists guard passes, `helm get values` is then denied by the read-only kubeconfig (cannot read release Secrets), and get_helm_args:107 raises an uncaught RuntimeError. Same defect as the test phase's carded pre-existing finding, but it now also hits the single-release invocation the P3 done-record names as its gate, so a later agent following that record will read a permissions crash as a broken release. Pre-image it 404'd instead; nothing in this slice's diff caused either.

Charts: the nginx:alpine base layer's stock `index.html` and `50x.html` still ship in the served docroot — both confirmed 200 on the live https://charts.home. Cosmetic only (helm fetches /index.yaml and the tarball URLs, never these), and the P2 r1 reviewer already logged it as advisory; a one-line `RUN rm` in the Dockerfile closes it whenever the repo is next touched. Note the P3 plan bullet's related prediction is falsified live: `/` returns 404, not the welcome page, because `location / { try_files $uri =404; }` bypasses the index directive.
